post_title: What will net outlays by the US government be in millions of dollars in FY 2028?

question.title: What will net outlays by the US government be in millions of dollars in FY 2028?
question.description:
Net outlays are the actual cash paid out by the US federal government in a given year, the equivalent of cash accounting. The Congressional Budget Office (CBO) [defines](https://budgetcounsel.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/10/page-77-78.pdf) outlays as:

> The issuance of checks, disbursement of cash, or electronic transfer of funds made to liquidate a federal obligation. Outlays also occur when interest on the Treasury debt held by the public accrues and when the government issues bonds, notes, debentures, monetary credits, or other cash-equivalent instruments in order to liquidate obligations. Also, under credit reform, the credit subsidy cost is recorded as an outlay when a direct or guaranteed loan is disbursed. An outlay is not recorded for repayment of debt principal, disbursements to the public by federal credit programs for direct loan obligations and loan guarantee commitments made in fiscal year 1992 or later, disbursements from deposit funds, and refunds of receipts that result from overpayments. Outlays during a fiscal year may be for payment of obligations incurred in prior years (prior-year obligations) or in the same year. Outlays, therefore, flow in part from unexpended balances of prior-year budgetary resources and in part from budgetary resources provided for the year in which the money is spent.

In 2024, federal government outlays were \$6.75 trillion and made up 23% of the US's Gross Domestic Product (GDP). On January 20, 2025, Donald J. Trump was inaugurated as the 47th US President, and that same day he [established](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/01/establishing-and-implementing-the-presidents-department-of-government-efficiency/) the Department of Governmental Efficiencey (DOGE), headed by Elon Musk. Musk has [stated a goal](https://www.yahoo.com/news/elon-musk-and-doge-promised-up-to-2-trillion-in-government-savings-how-much-have-they-actually-saved-so-far-201718142.html) of saving up to \$2 trillion annual expenditures by 2026. At the time of this question, the [DOGE website](https://doge.gov/savings) has tallied \$130 billion in savings.

In FY 2024, federal budget allocations [were](https://www.visualcapitalist.com/breaking-down-the-u-s-governments-2024-fiscal-year/) as follows:

| Function                      | Amount      |
| ----------------------------- | ----------- |
| Social Security               | \$1,461     |
| Health                        | \$912       |
| Net Interest                  | \$882       |
| Medicare                      | \$874       |
| National Defense              | \$874       |
| Income Security               | \$671       |
| Veterans' Benefits & Services | \$325       |
| Education                     | \$305       |
| Transportation                | \$137       |
| Other                         | \$311       |
| **Total Outlays**             | **\$6,752** |

In addition to the efforts of DOGE to cut outlays, the US Congress, of which both Houses are under Republican control at the time of this question, is working on the next budget under Senate reconciliation rules. Please see the [2025 Reconciliation Tracker](https://www.crfb.org/blogs/2025-reconciliation-tracker) by the Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget. See also from the Wharton School of Business at the University of Pennsylvania: [The FY2025 House Budget reconciliation and Trump Administration Tax Proposals: Budgetary, Economic, and Distributional Effects](https://budgetmodel.wharton.upenn.edu/issues/2025/2/27/fy2025-house-budget-reconciliation-and-trump-tax-proposals-effects)
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as the amount of [Federal Net Outlays](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/FYONET) in the United States in millions of dollars in Fiscal Year 2028, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED).
question.fine_print:
This question will resolve as the number shown by FRED, which represents millions of USD. For example, in 2024, this question would have resolved as **6,751,552**, as the net outlays were \$6,751,552,000,000. Therefore, when viewing the resolution source, please ensure (via the Edit Graph button) that:

* *Units* are set to **Millions of Dollars**.
* *Frequency* is set to Annual, Fiscal Year.

This question resolves based upon the first update by FRED incorporating federal net outlays for FY 2028. Further revisions after this question has been resolved will not be considered.
